evidence: G-S30. I judged the draft "Have you got any sense of what it is that's making it feel fake?" as the first sentence under the heading "It feels fake", against the words it replaces ("Do you have a sense of what it is that feels fake?") and his published line ("First ask what feels fake: the wording, the image, the expectation, or the role you’re trying to perform."). Does what the_change says: CONTEXT.txt holds the draft once, character for character as in DRAFT.txt, as the one sentence swapped in place; the rest of the paragraph is untouched. Meaning: still one diagnostic question asking the reader to find what makes the exercise feel fake, and the unchanged next sentence ("The words, an image, what you are expecting to get from this, a role you feel you have to play etc.") still answers it as a list of candidates, which fits "making it feel fake" at least as well as the old wording. The only shift is from "what feels fake" to "what is making it feel fake"; the candidates (words, image, expectation, role) are the same, and no new claim or fact appears. "Any sense" is a softer hedge, and the next sentence ("It doesn't matter that you don't have an inner voice/image to do this") agrees with it. Reads right in its context: as the section's opening question it follows from the heading (the writer's T03 note cites a sentence before it; there is none, but the heading does the setting up). Pronouns: the first "it" is the cleft ("what it is that"); the second "it" ("making it feel fake") is the practice the heading's "It" names, and the same paragraph then uses "this" / "do this" for it, so the referent is visible and nothing points at the wrong thing (C02 absent). "Have you got" is spoken and casual and sits fine in this section's voice. The apostrophe in "that's" is straight, like the "doesn't" and "don't" in the same paragraph (the section's one curly apostrophe, "aren’t", is in existing text further down). Tell rows: none PRESENT. I looked hardest at T15: the skeleton "... sense of what it is that ... fake?" is kept while "Do you have a" / "feels" become "Have you got any" / "is making it feel", but this is not the tell, because the replaced sentence carries no other tell for a swap to hide and the new one recasts the clause as a cause in the way a person would say it, rather than swapping in less likely synonyms. T24 and T19 (a question followed at once by a list): the list is the menu of candidate answers from his own published line for the reader to try on themselves, not a payoff built for suspense, and the question has its own job, so neither is present. T26: "feel fake" echoes the heading, which is the section's subject, and the echo ties the question to the heading. T22: it is a diagnostic question, not reassurance. T13, T09, T14: one plain sentence replaced where it stood, nothing reordered or moved, and the noticing in the paragraph ("it isn't necessarily about not having a 'grown up' or resisting doing the work", the protecting part) is his and unchanged. T01, C03, C04: no first person and no claim about anyone or anything. T27: no tic words. Linter: "D9 follows the source order" accepted, because the change is one sentence replaced where it stood, so agreement 1.00 is automatic, and T13/T09 were checked as above. "E36/E41 heavy second person" accepted: 7.1 per 100 is one "you" in a 14-word question to the reader (the replaced question had one in 12 words, about 8.3 per 100, so the draft is no heavier), the guide speaks to the reader as "you" throughout, and a question to the reader needs it; it is not coach reassurance.
